text:
Just wanted to share a positive experience at the Hadera Population Authority office, since I had read many stressful stories before going and I was honestly expecting the worst.

We had an appointment at 9:00 and were allowed in about 5 minutes early. We got a number and were called after around 15 minutes. The clerk who handled our case was very kind and helpful.

Our case was a bit complicated because our appointment had been postponed/cancelled several times due to the security situation, and by the time we finally had the appointment there had already been a gap in my visa. I was also within the 45-day period mentioned in a Bituach Leumi letter, so I was worried about losing residency/health insurance rights.

At first they could not find all the documents we had uploaded online, because they had been uploaded many months earlier. Luckily, we had brought some updated documents printed on paper, and I also had all the files with me digitally. In the end, we gave them the printed documents we had, and I sent the rest to their printer so they could add everything to the physical file.

One important thing we learned: even if you upload documents online, bring printed copies too. They told us they work with paper files, so it is better not to rely only on the online upload.

Because this was our first time at the Hadera branch after moving from another branch, they said we need to do an interview, which is mandatory. They scheduled the interview for the first week of September. However, because of my situation with Bituach Leumi and the visa gap, they issued the visa already at this appointment (before the interview and the missing documents). I also requested an intervisa, and they put the stickers in my passport.

They told me that my new teudat zehut should arrive in about three weeks, but that I can travel with my passport because the visa is already in it. For the next interview, we need to bring the remaining updated documents, including friends’ letters.

Another detail that may be useful: my passport expires in around 15 months, so I did not have the full two years of validity they usually ask for. The clerk still gave me a one-year visa, but told me that for the next renewal I should bring a renewed passport.

Overall, I was very nervous before the appointment, but the experience was much better than expected. The staff member was kind, practical, and actually tried to help. I think it is also important to share the good experiences, not only the bad ones :)
